Protect the aircraft and payload first, even if doing so extends flight above exposed people.
Continue the automated mission until software selects a landing point; crew communication can wait.
Climb vertically over the crowd so the remote PIC has more time to diagnose the fault.
explanation: Protect exposed people: maneuver/land/terminate toward the safest area, communicate, secure the site and preserve/report evidence as applicable. This assesses Emergency procedures for operations over people.

prompt: What changes in a night emergency?
choices: Reduced cues and unlit obstacles narrow options, requiring surveyed alternates, lighting, crew calls, and avoidance of blind automated routes.
Night removes visual distractions and makes an unsurveyed straight-line automated return safer.
Anti-collision lighting reveals every obstacle, so daylight site surveys and alternate landings are unnecessary.
The emergency response is unchanged because the controller display supplies all legally required visual information.
explanation: Reduced visual cues and unlit obstacles constrain options; use surveyed alternates, lighting and crew callouts, avoiding a blind automated route. This assesses Emergency procedures for night operations.

prompt: What makes team communication effective?
choices: Standard callouts, closed-loop acknowledgements, shared plans, explicit roles and handoffs, and authority for anyone to call abort.
Minimal callouts, assumed acknowledgements, flexible unspoken roles, and abort authority limited to the client.
Independent crew plans with no handoff language, preventing one person's concern from delaying the mission.
Continuous conversation about nonessential tasks so silence never distracts the remote PIC.
explanation: Standard callouts, closed-loop acknowledgement, shared plan, explicit roles/handoffs and authority for anyone to call an abort. This assesses Effective team communication.

prompt: How should task saturation be managed?
choices: Maintain aircraft control first, shed nonessential work, delegate, slow or hold, land if needed, and avoid fixation.
Complete camera and client tasks first, then restore aircraft awareness after workload falls.
Increase task pace and stop crew callouts so the remote PIC can handle every item personally.
Continue the route unchanged because automation prevents saturation from affecting flight safety.
explanation: Aviate/maintain control first, shed nonessential mission tasks, delegate, slow/hold/land and avoid fixation. This assesses Task management.

prompt: Can a pilot operate after eight hours if still impaired?
choices: No; eight hours is only one restriction, and any remaining impairment or applicable BAC or drug effect still prohibits operation.
Yes; exactly eight hours after drinking, all other alcohol and impairment restrictions automatically end.
Yes, if BAC is below 0.08%, even when judgment or reaction time remains impaired.
No, because Part 107 imposes a universal 24-hour prohibition after any alcohol consumption.
explanation: No. Eight hours is only one restriction; any alcohol/drug impairment remains disqualifying, as do applicable BAC and medication effects. This assesses Drug and alcohol use.

prompt: How should hyperventilation be handled?
choices: Reduce workload, consciously slow breathing, land, and seek medical help if symptoms persist or the cause is uncertain.
Breathe faster and deeper while continuing the mission so oxygen reaches the brain more quickly.
Hold the breath until tingling stops, then resume high-workload flight without landing.
Assume all dizziness is hyperventilation and avoid medical evaluation even if symptoms persist.
explanation: Recognize rapid breathing/dizziness/tingling, reduce workload, consciously slow breathing and land; seek medical help when symptoms persist or diagnosis is uncertain. This assesses Hyperventilation.

prompt: What is added to a night preflight?
choices: Check anti-collision light function, visibility, and mounting; orientation cues; displays and flashlights; unlit obstacles; and survey assumptions.
Check only battery percentage because daytime preflight covers every lighting and visual-cue issue.
Maximize display brightness and skip obstacle review because anti-collision lights illuminate the route.
Verify runway lights and ADS-B Out instead of the aircraft's lighting, visual cues, and alternate areas.
explanation: Verify anti-collision light function/visibility/secure mounting, aircraft orientation cues, display/flashlights, unlit obstacles and daylight-survey assumptions. This assesses Night-operation preflight inspection.

topic: Manufacturer Declaration of Compliance for Category 2 and 3

The pilot should submit a new declaration after every flight rather than verify the producer's accepted one.
